question: Identify the state abbreviations where, for both male and female legislators, the retention rate remains greater than zero at specific intervals of 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, and 10 years after their first term start date. A legislator is considered retained if they are serving on December 31 of the respective year. Only include states where both gender cohorts maintain non-zero retention rates at all six of these time points during the first decade of service.
sql:
-- Final result: states where both M and F have non-zero retention at all 6 intervals
WITH first_terms AS (
    SELECT lt.id_bioguide, lt.term_start, lt.term_end, lt.state,
           l.gender
    FROM legislators_terms lt
    JOIN legislators l ON lt.id_bioguide = l.id_bioguide
    WHERE lt.term_number = 0
),
intervals AS (
    SELECT 0 AS interval UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 4 UNION ALL SELECT 6 UNION ALL SELECT 8 UNION ALL SELECT 10
),
retention_check AS (
    SELECT 
        ft.id_bioguide,
        ft.state,
        ft.gender,
        i.interval,
        DATE_TRUNC('year', CAST(ft.term_start AS DATE)) + (i.interval * INTERVAL '1 year') + INTERVAL '1 year' - INTERVAL '1 day' AS dec31_date
    FROM first_terms ft
    CROSS JOIN intervals i
),
retained AS (
    SELECT 
        rc.id_bioguide,
        rc.state,
        rc.gender,
        rc.interval,
        rc.dec31_date,
        CASE WHEN EXISTS (
            SELECT 1 FROM legislators_terms lt2 
            WHERE lt2.id_bioguide = rc.id_bioguide
            AND CAST(lt2.term_start AS DATE) <= rc.dec31_date
            AND CAST(lt2.term_end AS DATE) >= rc.dec31_date
        ) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_retained
    FROM retention_check rc
),
state_gender_intervals AS (
    SELECT state, gender, interval, 
           1.0 * SUM(is_retained) / COUNT(*) as retention_rate
    FROM retained
    GROUP BY state, gender, interval
),
state_gender_valid AS (
    SELECT state, gender,
           SUM(CASE WHEN retention_rate > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as valid_intervals
    FROM state_gender_intervals
    GROUP BY state, gender
),
valid_states AS (
    SELECT sg1.state
    FROM state_gender_valid sg1
    JOIN state_gender_valid sg2 ON sg1.state = sg2.state AND sg1.gender != sg2.gender
    WHERE sg1.valid_intervals = 6 AND sg2.valid_intervals = 6
)
SELECT DISTINCT vs.state
FROM valid_states vs
ORDER BY vs.state
